title: My PhD Interview at the University of Isfahan
excerpt: My PhD interview at the University of Isfahan was short, a bit bitter, and interesting. I was accepted, but I turned it down to give myself a chance to apply abroad.

blocks.text: The University of Isfahan, a strange interview, bitter, sweet... I don't know.
For the University of Isfahan, which is my current university for my master's, I had registered for both Software PhD and Artificial Intelligence.
The first day was the Software PhD interview and I had been invited and I arrived earlier than the time. When I entered most of the professors were seated and I also presented my forms to them.

Well, they were familiar with me and I also explained the path I had taken. The interview wasn't hard but one of the professors started to make the interview a bit harder (honestly I wasn't prepared for it either).

He said what did you learn in the machine learning course? And I, who had finished this course a year ago, really didn't remember its syllabus, but well as much as I remembered I said: there were different paradigms of machine learning and...
And then he said: what does paradigm mean? I said I don't know.

He said explain Back Propagation, I gave a broken and incomplete explanation and in the end he said is it the first derivative or the second? And I had gotten so nervous that I said I don't know, just to let it go.
The other professors also asked what topics do you like to work on in the future and... which was simple.
The interview was also short, at most it lasted 15 minutes.
Anyway, it was a very good interview, a bit bitter and interesting.
In the end I was accepted but because of the conditions I had, the war conditions, and the opportunity I wanted to give myself for applying, I rejected this offer to see what will happen.
